findings.title: Upsampling eligibility check uses the wrong dataset variable
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, the function parameter is named `scoped_dataset` (the dataset actually being queried for this specific call), but the eligibility check calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` using the outer closed-over `dataset` variable from `get()` instead of the local `scoped_dataset` parameter. In the simple path these happen to be equal, but `get_event_stats_factory`'s `fn` calls `_get_event_stats` with different dataset values (e.g. `discover` for the errors-only/transactions-only split queries, or `split_dataset`) when handling dashboard-widget discover splitting. In those calls, the upsampling decision is computed against the wrong dataset, so the `count()`→`upsampled_count()` transform can be incorrectly applied or skipped for the dataset that is actually executed, producing inconsistent/incorrect counts for dashboard widgets using the discover-split code path.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called anywhere
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is introduced with a docstring stating it 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency', but nothing in this PR (or apparently the rest of the codebase) calls it. As written, it is dead code, and the 60-second eligibility cache set in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` has no actual invalidation path wired to allowlist option changes. This either means the function is unused dead code that should be removed, or an integration point (e.g. an options-changed signal handler) is missing, leaving stale upsampling decisions for up to 60 seconds with no way to force a refresh.

findings.title: Cache key built from hash() of project id tuple risks collisions
findings.body: The cache key `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"` relies on Python's built-in `hash()` of an integer tuple to disambiguate different project-id sets within the same organization. Hash collisions between distinct tuples are possible (hash() truncates to a fixed-width integer), which could cause one set of projects to incorrectly reuse another set's cached eligibility result for up to 60 seconds, silently enabling or disabling upsampling for the wrong query. A deterministic string key built from the sorted ids directly (e.g. joined by commas) would avoid this risk entirely and is no more expensive.

findings.title: New upsampled_count() function is public, bypassing allowlist gating
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction is registered without `private=True`, unlike other internal-only aggregate functions in the same converter. This means any user can directly type `upsampled_count()` in a Discover/Events query, bypassing the allowlist check in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`/`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` entirely. Depending on how `sample_weight` is populated for non-allowlisted projects (NULL vs default value), this could either return misleading data or raise a SQL error (e.g. converting NULL to a non-nullable Int64), since the function assumes sample_weight is always present 'per our data model requirements' — an assumption the public API doesn't enforce.

findings.title: Stray gitlink/submodule artifact added to the repository
findings.body: A new top-level entry `sentry-repo` is added that is a gitlink pointing to commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a` (the PR's own base commit), with no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry shown in the diff. This looks like an accidental artifact from a bad rebase/squash or local tooling leftover rather than an intentional change. Committing a dangling gitlink with no submodule registration can confuse `git status`/`git submodule` tooling and CI checkout steps, and should be removed before merge.

findings.title: No tests for the public cached entry point or cache invalidation
findings.body: The test file only exercises the private helpers `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, and `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`. The PR's headline feature — the 60-second caching behavior in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (cache hit/miss paths, correct bool-vs-None handling) — and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` are never directly unit tested. Given the PR title explicitly calls out 'performance optimizations' via caching, the caching logic itself (the riskiest new behavior) has no dedicated test coverage.

findings.title: Misleading/contradictory docstring about cache freshness
findings.body: The docstring of `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` states the function 'reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state.' In reality, its caller `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` wraps this function's result in a 60-second cache, so the configuration is not read fresh on every call — only on cache misses. This contradicts the stated intent and could mislead future maintainers into believing allowlist changes take effect immediately, when in fact they can be delayed up to 60 seconds.

findings.title: Test helper overloads generic 'sample_rate' field and silently swallows all errors
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` writes into the generic top-level `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` key whenever `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` is present, for any event type processed by `store_event` (not just errors). This repurposes a field name that is also used elsewhere in Sentry for transaction/dynamic sampling semantics, risking ambiguity if both mechanisms ever intersect on the same event. Additionally, both exception-handling blocks use bare `except Exception: pass`, silently discarding malformed `client_sample_rate` values or unexpected `contexts` shapes, which can mask bugs in tests relying on this helper instead of surfacing a clear failure.

findings.title: Transform only matches exact 'count()' string, silently ignoring aliased forms
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` only rewrites a column when its lowercased/stripped value equals exactly `"count()"`. Any other valid representation of the same aggregate — e.g. `"count() as total"`, or `count()` embedded in an equation — is left untouched with no warning or fallback, so the request silently uses the raw (non-upsampled) count. There is no test covering this partial-match limitation, and callers have no way to know the transform was skipped for their specific column form.
